title_ar: منبر الخميس يستضيف فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء
title_en: The Thursday Platform Hosts His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, Head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars
body_ar: استضاف منبر الخميس مساء اليوم بمسجد أبي طلحة في انواكشوط سماحة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو في محاضرة تحت عنوان : " اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى " حيث استهل سماحة الشيخ حديثه قائلا : إن العدل من القيم الأساسية للإنسان وبه قامت السموات والأرض ، ولذلك أمر الله به أمرا مطلقا يتناول جميع المأمورين ، مبرزا أن من أهم مظاهره المساواة في أداء الحقوق الكثيرة والتي تشمل على وجه الخصوص حقوق الله وحقوق النفس وحقوق الأمة وحقوق الجيران ، وقد أكد الشيخ على أن الإنسان مطالب بالعدل في أداء هذه الحقوق كلها عدلا يقتضي إيصالها إلى مستحقيها ، كما تطرق سماحته إلى مجالات العدل ، منبها إلى أهميته في مجال الحكم بالذات ، حيث ذكر أن هناك من يوالون الحكام ، فيحاولون تبرير أخطائهم والتماس العذر لهم في كل ما يقعون فيه ، ويبالغون في ذلك حتى يصلوا إلى ماوصل إليه الباطنية من الشيعة الذين بحثوا : هل الحاكم مكلف أم لا ، ورأوا أنه يرتفع عنه قلم التكليف بمجرد توليه للعدل ، وقد أوضح سماحته أن هذا خطأ فادح ، وبين أن الحكام أخطاؤهم كبيرة فمن عمل منهم عملا وأشهره في الإعلام فلا يمكن أن يلتمس له العذر ، بل لابد أن يبين له خطؤه وأن يرد عليه ، كما ذكر أيضا أن وسائل الإعلام مطالبة – هي الأخرى - بالعدل فيما تكتب وتنشر سواء تعلق الأمر بالحكام أو غيرهم ، هذا وقد بين الشيخ أنه من العدل أن يصرف الإنسان عن مكان بقي فيه مدة إلى مكان آخر ليبدأ من جديد فيحتاج إلى ابتكار وإبداع ، وحينئذ يجدد حياته وهذا ما تحتاجه البشرية على الدوام . واختتم سماحته المحاضرة بالتأكيد على مظهر مهم من مظاهر العدل ألا وهو اختيار الناس على أساس الكفاءات ، مشددا على أن من تمام العدل في الدول أن لايولى على وظيفة إلا من كان من أهلها والعارفين بها ، وإذاعدل عن ذلك فسيقع الاختلال لا محالة .
body_en:
The Thursday Platform this evening hosted, at the Abu Talhah Mosque in Nouakchott, his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, in a lecture under the title "Be just; that is nearer to God-consciousness". His eminence the Sheikh opened his address by saying that justice is among the fundamental values of the human being, and that by it the heavens and the earth stand; and that God therefore commanded it with an unqualified command taking in all who are commanded. He brought out that among its most important manifestations is equality in the discharge of the many rights, which include in particular the rights of God, the rights of the self, the rights of the community and the rights of neighbours. The Sheikh affirmed that a person is required to observe justice in discharging all of these rights — a justice that requires their delivery to those entitled to them.

His eminence also dealt with the domains of justice, drawing attention to its importance in the domain of rule in particular. He mentioned that there are those who give their allegiance to rulers and try to justify their errors and to find excuses for them in everything they fall into, and who go so far in this that they arrive at what the Batiniyyah among the Shia arrived at, who investigated whether the ruler is under legal obligation or not, and held that the pen of legal obligation is lifted from him by the mere fact of his taking charge of justice. His eminence made clear that this is a grave error, and explained that rulers' errors are great: whoever among them performs an act and publicises it in the media cannot have an excuse sought for him; rather his error must be made plain to him and he must be answered. He also mentioned that the media, for their part, are required to observe justice in what they write and publish, whether the matter concerns rulers or others.

The Sheikh further explained that it is part of justice that a person be moved on from a post he has held for a period to another, so that he may begin afresh and will need invention and origination; and at that point he renews his life, and this is what humankind stands in need of at all times. His eminence closed the lecture by affirming an important manifestation of justice, namely the choosing of people on the basis of competence, stressing that part of the completeness of justice in states is that no one be appointed to a post except one who is fit for it and knowledgeable in it; and that if that is departed from, dysfunction will inevitably occur.

flags.arabic: حتى يصلوا إلى ماوصل إليه الباطنية من الشيعة الذين بحثوا : هل الحاكم مكلف أم لا
flags.context: the comparison drawn in the section on justice in the domain of rule
options: translate exactly and attribute the position only as narrowly as the summary does
render 'الباطنية من الشيعة' more generally as 'the esotericists among the Shia'
flags.note: Editorially sensitive on two counts. It is sectarian: a named Shia sub-group is used as the limiting case of a doctrine, and in English out of context this reads as a characterisation of Shia belief generally, which the Arabic does not say — it names the Batiniyyah specifically. And it is political: the point of the comparison is a criticism of those who make excuses for rulers, delivered in Nouakchott in March 2011. The English keeps the attribution exactly as narrow as the Arabic makes it and adds nothing. All of it is the site editor's summary of a spoken lecture.

flags.arabic: يرتفع عنه قلم التكليف بمجرد توليه للعدل
flags.context: the doctrine attributed to the Batiniyyah
options: by the mere fact of his taking charge of justice
by the mere fact of his assuming rule
by his being appointed to administer justice
flags.note: 'توليه للعدل' is awkward as served: the argument requires the ruler's assumption of authority, not of 'justice', and a word may have shifted or dropped. Rendered close to the Arabic so the awkwardness stays visible rather than being resolved into a reading the source does not support. The whole clause reports a doctrine the Sheikh rejects, and must not be read as his own.

flags.arabic: من العدل أن يصرف الإنسان عن مكان بقي فيه مدة إلى مكان آخر
options: render exactly, as a general point about renewal in office
read it as a comment on a particular office or officeholder
flags.note: Rendered as the general proposition the summary makes it. Note the date: Nouakchott, 31 March 2011. A statement that justice requires moving people on from posts they have long held reads very differently in that month than as an abstract principle of administration, and it will be quoted as a comment on incumbency. Nothing has been added and nothing softened; the date should be displayed with it.

flags.context: missing word spaces at three points
flags.note: Three missing word spaces, all left as served in body_ar. Together with similar defects elsewhere in this slice they indicate the news items were typed quickly and not proofread.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh; the reporting frame is preserved throughout.

The lecture title is the Qur'anic phrase at Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:8; it is rendered in English inside the title rather than braced as a quotation, because it functions here as a title and the source does not present it as a citation.

The page ends with a navigation line inviting the reader to click through to the recording in the site's separate media system; it is a site affordance rather than content and is not part of body_ar or body_en.
